item.lead: These notes close the first section.

perform.markdown:
The script models text one character at a time. It maps each character to an integer, so it does not use GPT-2's BPE tokens. Before it can do that, it needs the whole corpus as text. The step produces one Python string, and it comes first because every later step works from that string.

How the lines do it:

- **A guarded download.** The file path is built next to the script. The check on line 14 asks whether the file already exists, and the request is made only if it does not. A second run finds the file and skips the request, so the download happens once.
- **One full read.** Line 20 opens the file and reads all of it into a single string. It does not split by line or by word. The string's length counts characters, and that includes spaces and newlines.
- **The number to remember.** The recorded run says the string is 1,115,394 characters long. Every later count starts from that number.

A check you can do: later, the text will be cut into two parts of 1,003,854 and 111,540 characters. Add them: 1,003,854 + 111,540 = 1,115,394. The split loses nothing.

Terms introduced:

- **Character-level modeling:** the model's units are single characters, not subword tokens.
- **Corpus:** the whole body of training text.
- **Raw text:** the corpus as one unsplit string.

Hand-over: the text now sits in one string. Next, you will find which distinct characters it contains.
